description: Ashley explains Bjarne’s emotional withdrawal and isolation. C10 can be discovered after C09 or through a more direct question.

openingMessages.speaker: Ashley
openingMessages.text: Can I tell you something? Something I've been wanting to say for a while?

choices.text: Of course. I'm listening.
I know I haven't been very emotionally available.
I was working hard. I was trying to build a future.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I miss talking to you. Not just about what happened at work, or what you're building, or what needs fixing.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I miss hearing about what you're thinking. What you're excited about. What you're worried about. What makes you happy.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: You used to tell me those things. But somewhere along the way, you stopped.

choices.text: I stopped talking about how I felt?
Was I really that difficult to talk to?
I think I understand what you mean.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: That's one way to describe it.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: You were there physically, but it felt like you were somewhere else.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I stopped knowing what you were thinking. I stopped knowing how you were feeling.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: Eventually, I stopped knowing whether you even wanted me around.

choices.text: I didn't realize it had become that bad.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I know you were. And I never asked you to stop caring about your work.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I just wanted you to care about something besides it.

choices.text: I think I stopped letting people know what I was feeling.
I didn't know how to balance everything.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: Yes. Whenever something bothered you, you'd just say you were fine.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: Whenever I asked how you were feeling, you'd change the subject.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I felt like I was standing right next to you, but you wouldn't let me in.

choices.text: Was I only like this with you, or had I been pulling away from everyone?
Did I have many friends?
I'm sorry. I wish I'd let you in.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: It wasn't that you were difficult.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: It was that I never knew what was going on inside your head. I wanted to be there for you, but you wouldn't let me.

choices.text: Was I only like this with you, or had I been pulling away from everyone?
Did I have many friends?
I think I understand.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I hope so. Because I really did try.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I didn't need you to solve everything. I just wanted you to let me know you were struggling.

choices.text: Was I only like this with you, or had I been pulling away from everyone?
Did I have many friends?
Thank you for telling me.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I know. It felt like you were somewhere else even when you were right beside me.

choices.text: Was I only like this with you, or had I been pulling away from everyone?

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: Everyone, Bjarne. That's what worried me.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: You barely saw anyone outside of work. You had Mark, mostly.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I honestly can't think of many other people you were still close to.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: You used to have a whole circle of friends. But one by one, you'd stop replying, cancel plans, or just tell people you were too busy.

choices.text: So Mark was really the only person I kept in touch with?
Why didn't anyone say anything?
I guess I didn't make it very easy for people to stay.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: That's a strange question.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: You had Mark, obviously. But honestly, by the end, I wasn't sure who else you were talking to.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: You stopped making plans with people, stopped responding to messages... It was like your entire world had become work.

choices.text: I didn't realize I'd pushed so many people away.
So Mark was really the only person I kept in touch with?

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: Pretty much. You two have always been close. I think he was one of the few people who kept trying even when you stopped making an effort.

choices.text: I should make more of an effort with him.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: People did, Bjarne. I did. Your mother did, too.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: But you always had a reason why things could wait until later.

choices.text: I wish I'd listened.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: Maybe not. But that doesn't mean you can't change things.

choices.text: I want to try.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I know. I just wish you'd let someone help you carry it.

choices.text: I think I need to learn how.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I don't know what happens next, Bjarne. I just hope you start making time for the people who care about you. Not because you owe us anything. Just because you deserve to have a life outside of work.

choices.text: Thank you for telling me all of this.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: I don't know what happens next, Bjarne.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: But I hope you figure things out. And I hope you start making time for the people who care about you.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: Not because you owe us anything. Just because you deserve to have a life outside of work.

lines.speaker: Grand Architect
lines.text: A system can pass every test and still fail the people depending on it.

lines.speaker: Pragmatist
lines.text: ...I hate when the serious one makes a good point.

lines.speaker: Detective
lines.text: We've found the pattern. The question is no longer what happened that weekend. It's why Bjarne was so desperate to escape his own life.

choices.text: I think I'd like that.
I don't know if I remember how.
Thank you for telling me all of this.

lines.speaker: Ashley
lines.text: Then maybe that's somewhere to start. Take care of yourself, okay?
